grammar.title: The Subjunctive after Opinion Verbs and Conjunctions
grammar.explanation: In Italian, verbs of opinion (pensare, credere, ritenere) and concessive conjunctions (sebbene, benché, nonostante) require the subjunctive in the subordinate clause: 'Penso che sia giusto' (I think it is right), 'Sebbene faccia freddo, esco' (Although it is cold, I go out). Connectors like 'tuttavia', 'quindi', 'inoltre', and 'invece' do NOT trigger the subjunctive as they connect independent clauses. The key is distinguishing between conjunctions that require subjunctive (sebbene, affinché, prima che) and connectors that do not (tuttavia, quindi, perciò).
